title: Knowledge check: Classic ASP Architecture

questions.prompt: Which subtopic is explicitly listed under “Classic ASP Architecture” in the attached Classic ASP curriculum?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists “Browser and web-server responsibilities” under lesson 5, “Classic ASP Architecture”. The distractors belong to other lesson topics.

questions.prompt: When applying “Classic ASP Architecture” in a legacy Classic ASP application, which approach is strongest?
options: Assume every value from a browser is trustworthy.
Enable detailed errors for all public visitors.
Change several settings at once and infer which one fixed the issue.
Make the runtime assumptions explicit and test normal, invalid, and boundary values.
questions.answer_key: Make the runtime assumptions explicit and test normal, invalid, and boundary values.
questions.explanation: This approach keeps classic asp architecture testable and respects Classic ASP/IIS runtime boundaries. The exact IIS, provider, or component behavior must be checked in the target test environment.

questions.prompt: Before marking work on “Classic ASP Architecture” ready for review, what evidence should be recorded?
options: Delete diagnostic evidence before recording the outcome.
Treat a successful happy-path test as proof of all security properties.
Document the observed result, tool/runtime version, and one meaningful failure or edge case.
Claim the production deployment passed without running it.
questions.answer_key: Document the observed result, tool/runtime version, and one meaningful failure or edge case.
questions.explanation: Good maintenance evidence includes the expected and observed result, relevant version/runtime assumptions, and a boundary or failure test. Never claim an execution/deployment test that was not run.
